title: Typedefs and type aliases
recap: A type alias gives an existing type another name; it does not create a distinct type. A domain name such as Cents can clarify what a number represents without changing arithmetic rules.
Units and rounding remain part of your contract. Keep money in integer minor units when that is the required representation, and specify what happens to fractional minor units.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: The Cents alias names long long. Implement discountedPrice(price, percent): return price times (100-percent) / 100 in integer cents, discarding any fractional cent. Return -1 for negative price or percent outside [0,100]. Prices are at most 1000000, so multiplication fits Cents.
hints: Use Cents for the result and intermediate price arithmetic.
Subtract the discount from 100 to find the kept percentage.
Multiply before dividing to avoid unnecessary truncation.
